item.text: I’ll use the supplied Deep Research Council skill to check both vendors against the three gates and trace the published WDRI scores to their source. I’ll use only the packet.

**Select CargoLoop for the limited deployment.** Its trailing 12-month availability was 99.92%, above the 99.9% minimum. Its acceptance test demonstrated WMS API v2 reads and writes for both inventory and orders. Its submission reports full export of inventory, orders and audit records in six calendar days, within the seven-day limit. (`SN-REQ` §1, `SN-VEND` §2)

Northstar met the availability and export gates at 99.98% and three days. Its API test demonstrated only reads, and write support is planned. Northstar’s lower three-year cost and shorter onboarding therefore cannot change the decision. Those preferences apply only among vendors that pass every gate. (`SN-VEND` §§1–2, `SN-REQ` §§1–2)

Give WDRI no weight in this award. It ranks Northstar 94/100 and CargoLoop 81/100 using automation (65%), worker satisfaction (30%) and subscription price (5%). Northstar sponsored the research and supplied platform information. The Alliance provides neither item-level data nor validation of the weights against buyer requirements. The regional register omits WDRI from its formal frameworks and leaves informal use open. (`SN-INDEX` §§1–2, `SN-REG` §1)

**Four publishers display the scores, but there is one underlying score origin and zero independent validations.** TradeTech, MarketOps and Northstar all reproduce the Alliance scorecard. Two newsletters bring the citation network to six publishers. Both also cite the Alliance. (`SN-INDEX` §§1–2, `SN-TRADE` §§1–2, `SN-CONSULT` §§1–2, `SN-VENDOR` §§1–2)
